stages.name: Irrational behaviour
stages.title: Irrational behaviour
stages.sub: See three ways real buyers depart from the rationality assumption.

steps.q: The rationality assumption says people weigh every option perfectly. In real life, do shoppers have unlimited time and brainpower to check every option, or only a limited amount?
steps.hint: Think about how long you actually spend comparing products in a shop.

steps.q: A new coffee shop opens next to one that has been empty for months. You see a long queue outside the new one and decide to join it without checking the menu. Are you weighing up your own costs and benefits, or copying what others are doing?
steps.wrong: Weighing up my own costs and benefits
steps.hint: Did you compare the two shops yourself, or just follow the crowd?

steps.q: You have bought the same brand of cereal every week for ten years. A cheaper, equally good brand appears next to it. Do you stop and recalculate which is best, or just pick up the usual box?
steps.right: Just pick up the usual box
steps.hint: Are you actually comparing the two boxes each week, or acting on routine?

steps.hint: Can most people multiply out a monthly rate into a true yearly cost in their head?
